It might have been much more simpler for $1 to be assert or deassert $2 be gpio and you go over the switch statement using
```
case "$1$2" in
  "assert2_cpu0-thermtrip-alert")
    do thermtrip assert things.
    ;;
  "deassert2_cpu0-thermtrip-alert")  
    do thermtrip deassert things.
    ;;
  "assert2_cpu0-prochot-alert")
    do prochot assert things.
    ;;
  "deassert2_cpu0-prochot-alert")
    do prochot deassert things.
    ;;
  esac
```
Having the *.service files pass in DeviceOverOperatingTemperatureFault or its variants is not really helping you clean up the code here in anyway. If you want assert/deassert, just pass that from the service to this script.

Why do we have to enumerate all of the combinations here?  That seems strange.

Can you at least make an "else" for unsupported?

[nit feel free to ignore] Looks like gpio_logging_valid other than checking if the gpio is a valid name (which it obviously is) is also checking if sgpio is in a valid state. https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/master/meta-facebook/meta-harma/recipes-phosphor/gpio/phosphor-gpio-monitor/logging-util#L22 and if so sleeping for 2s before continuing. If thats all we care about, can we just call sgpio_valid here? :-)

I think you are intending of resolving the event from DeviceOverOperatingTemperatureFault (gpio: thermtrip) which is a different GPIO than DeviceOverOperatingTemperature (gpio: prochot). So the STASH_FILE file here is not going to be the one from thermtrip as you might have intended since that explicitly uses the gpio name.

Was your intention:
prochot assert -> create DeviceOverOperatingTemperature
thermtrip assert -> create DeviceOverOperatingTemperatureFault
thermtrip deassert -> create resolve DeviceOverOperatingTemperatureFault
prochot deassert -> resolve DeviceOverOperatingTemperature, create DeviceOperatingNormalTemperature

yes that's the flow I want to have.
1.prochot assert -> create DeviceOverOperatingTemperature -> creates STASH_FILE /run/cpu0-prochot-alert.log_entry

2. thermtrip assert -> create DeviceOverOperatingTemperatureFault -> creates STASH_FILE /run/cpu0-thermtrip-alert.log_entry

3. thermtrip deassert -> resolve DeviceOverOperatingTemperatureFault -> delete 
STASH_FILE /run/cpu0-thermtrip-alert.log_entry and log DeviceOverOperatingTemperature

4. prochot deassert -> resolve DeviceOverOperatingTemperature -> delete STASH_FILE /run/cpu0-prochot-alert.log_entry and log DeviceOperatingNormalTemperature
